the mechanism by which insulin growth factor I stimulates the migration of smooth muscle cells.
understanding the molecular mechanisms that mediate the IGF-I stimulated cell migration.
the mechanisms by which growth factors stimulate the PI-3K pathway in SMCs, which are important for cell migration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SHP-2 plays an important role as a signaling molecule in mediating IGF-I-induced PI-3 kinase and Akt activation, and cell migration.

the SHP-2/p85 interaction is required for IGR-I stimulated cell migration.
the tyrosines in SHP-2 and p85 are required to activate the PI-3K pathway and cell migration.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the phosphatase SHP-2 plays an essential role in the regulation of PI-3 kinase and that this role is mediated, at least in part, through the interaction of SHP- 2 with the tyrosine residues on p85.
